2608.19083.title: When Readability and Source Retention Diverge: An Evaluability Gap in AI Translation
2608.19083.paper_summary: Readable AI output can leave an evaluability gap: even when the source is shown, an overall-quality judgment may not reflect what an output preserves. We investigated how source-text condition and output rendering relate to perceived translation quality, and how output and system appraisals relate to trust and stated disclosure willingness in a plain-text interface. A focal 2 * 2 comparison (N=306) using TransLingo examined simple generated narratives and complex literary-philosophical prose alongside LLM-generated readability-oriented outputs and researcher-revised fidelity-oriented outputs. A descriptive stimulus audit indicated greater source retention in fidelity-oriented outputs in both source-text conditions. Factorial analyses showed a significant rendering-by-source-text-condition interaction in perceived quality. Participants rated fidelity-oriented outputs higher than readability-oriented outputs for the simple narratives, whereas no reliable rendering difference emerged for the complex prose. A corresponding source-condition-dependent pattern was observed for perceived intelligence, agency-oriented anthropomorphic attribution, and task-performance trust. A separate theory-ordered appraisal-structure SEM characterized concurrent associations among perceived quality, perceived intelligence, agency-oriented anthropomorphic attribution, task-performance trust, and stated disclosure willingness across six domains, with task-performance trust as the proximal correlate of stated willingness. The observed rating pattern distinguishes source access from source evaluability: for the complex stimuli, displaying the source did not ensure that one overall-quality rating reflected differences in retained content. It also separates support for evaluating translation output from data-handling support for decisions about what personal text to entrust to a system.
2608.19083.paper_summary_zh: 可讀的 AI 輸出可能會留下可評估性差距：即使顯示了來源，整體質量評判也可能無法反映輸出所保留的內容。我們調查了來源文本條件和輸出呈現如何與感知的翻譯質量相關，以及輸出和系統評價如何與信任和在純文本介面中的披露意願相關。一項以 TransLingo 為基礎的焦點 2 * 2 比較（N=306）檢視了簡單生成的敘述和複雜的文學哲學散文，並與 LLM 生成的可讀性導向輸出和研究者修訂的忠實度導向輸出進行比較。一項描述性刺激審核顯示，在兩種來源文本條件下，忠實度導向輸出的來源保留率更高。因子分析顯示在感知質量上存在顯著的呈現與來源文本條件的交互作用。參與者對簡單敘述的忠實度導向輸出的評價高於可讀性導向輸出，而對於複雜散文則沒有出現可靠的呈現差異。對於感知智能、以代理為導向的人格化歸因和任務表現信任，觀察到了一個相應的來源條件依賴模式。一個單獨的理論有序評價結構 SEM 描述了在六個領域中感知質量、感知智能、以代理為導向的人格化歸因、任務表現信任和披露意願之間的同時關聯，其中任務表現信任是披露意願的近因相關因素。觀察到的評分模式區分了來源訪問與來源可評估性：對於複雜刺激，顯示來源並未確保整體質量評分反映保留內容的差異。它還將評估翻譯輸出的支持與對於決定將哪些個人文本託付給系統的數據處理支持分開。
